title: Student Welfare
metaDescription: Student welfare at Rosehill College — Te Whare Kimiora brings together our counselling team, registered nurses and Māori support (Kaimanaaki) to look after student wellbeing, health and safety.

sections.heading: Student welfare
sections.lede: At Rosehill College, the well-being of our students is our top priority. This page provides essential information and resources to support our students in various aspects of their school life.

sections.heading: Our canteen

image.alt: Food on offer at the Rosehill College canteen

sections.html:
Our canteen is currently operated by the school to ensure students continue to have access to fresh and affordable food options throughout the day.

Our menu includes a variety of hot meals, sandwiches, snacks, and drinks, with options rotating regularly and seasonally to suit student preferences. We aim to provide nutritious and convenient food choices to support student wellbeing and energy levels during the school day.

If you have any inquiries for the canteen, you can email canteen@rosehillcollege.school.nz.

sections.heading: Restorative practice

image.alt: Rosehill College students and staff talking together

sections.html: Restorative practices are best understood as a 'community response' to wrong-doing. This involves bringing together all of the people involved in an incident to understand how people have been affected, with a focus on putting it right.

sections.heading: Why is Rosehill College using this approach?
sections.html:
Educators are recognising that restorative practices have many advantages over punishment alone:

  • Restorative practices have a focus on people, not rules.
  • Restorative practices give victims a voice about how they want their case to be handled.
  • Restorative practices make students who offend accountable to the people they have hurt.
  • Restorative practices address the root cause of an issue, not just the symptoms.

How do restorative practices fit with our values? Perfectly! Rosehill College is a community of students, parents and staff — so having a community or hui response to wrong-doing is ideal. Restorative practices place a priority on protecting relationships and rebuilding them if they become damaged through a harmful incident. Restorative practices are built upon core values such as Respect, Responsibility and Caring — which match our own values.

sections.heading: Te Whare Kimiora

image.alt: The Te Whare Kimiora team at Rosehill College — the school counsellors and registered nurses

sections.html:
Me mahi tahi tātou mō te oranga o te katoa — we work together for the wellbeing of everyone.

Te Whare Kimiora is our health and wellbeing hub, based in M4 next to the nurses' clinic. It brings together our counselling team, registered nurses and Kaimanaaki (Māori support), so every student has somewhere safe to turn — whether they need to talk something through, see a nurse, or find the right support beyond school.

sections.heading: Our counselling team
sections.lede: Our counsellors are full members of the New Zealand Association of Counsellors (NZAC), receive regular supervision, and work alongside a wide range of agencies who can help with more complex needs.

items.title: What we can help with
items.html:
Our school-based health and wellbeing services are here to help students stay healthy, feel supported, and take part in school life.

The team provides a safe and welcoming place where students can talk about health concerns, receive appropriate care, ask questions, and get help when something is affecting their wellbeing or ability to learn.

Our aim is to make healthcare easier to access for students who may face barriers such as cost, transport, cultural concerns, or simply not knowing where to go for support.

items.title: How to get support
items.html:
Students can get in touch in whatever way feels easiest:

  • Email kimiora@rosehillcollege.school.nz
  • Fill in an Appointment Request Form — on the bookshelf in the counselling building
  • Drop in to Te Whare Kimiora (M4) during break times

Staff who are worried about a student can refer through the student's Head of House, who will follow up with the team.

items.title: Confidentiality and Consent
items.html:
Students' health information is managed in accordance with legal and professional requirements, including the Health Information Privacy Code.

Information shared with the health team is treated confidentially. There are circumstances where information may need to be shared to meet legal or safety requirements.

Where appropriate, we encourage students to involve their parents or caregivers in decisions about their health. We recognise, however, that having a trusted and confidential place to seek help can be an important part of supporting young people.

sections.heading: Our registered nurse team
sections.lede: The Health Centre sits alongside Te Whare Kimiora in M4. Our registered nurses provide free, confidential health care to help students stay well, attend school and thrive.

items.title: What our nurses do
items.html:
Our health team can support students with a range of health and wellbeing needs, including:

* General health concerns
* Injuries and accidents
* Medical concerns and ongoing health conditions
* Health checks and health education
* Emotional wellbeing and mental health support
* Healthy lifestyle and health promotion
* Support with managing health conditions at school
* Health advice and information
* Referral to other health and support services when needed

items.title: Year 9 Health Checks
items.html:
Year 9 students may be offered a health check covering their general physical and emotional wellbeing, lifestyle, and any health concerns they would like to discuss.

Where further support is needed, the health team can provide follow-up advice or help connect the student with an appropriate service.

items.title: Our Approach
items.html: Student health information is managed in line with legal and professional requirements, including the Health Information Privacy Code. Information is kept confidential and only shared with the student's consent, or where there is a legal or safety reason to do so. Where appropriate, we always encourage students to involve their parents or whānau.

sections.heading: Kaimanaaki — Māori support
sections.html: Our Kaimanaaki (Whaea Pare Matthews) provides support to Māori students and their whānau. The role of our Kaimanaaki is to provide support that allows Māori students to succeed to their potential.

items.text: Dr Khaleghian runs our Peer Support Programme with the help of teaching staff and 100–200 Student Advisors — trustworthy, friendly seniors from each House who train for two days over the summer holidays.
Once trained, Student Advisors welcome and support our Year 9 students on their very first day, right through Term One and beyond, helping them settle into life at Rosehill College.
There are always speciality support groups running for students. Drop in to Te Whare Kimiora to check what's on, or keep an eye on the Daily Notices.
